title: Oil Market is Attempting a System Reboot

facts.claim: Crude oil prices are back at near pre-war levels despite more than 100 days of conflict that closed the Strait of Hormuz.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: Recovery of Persian Gulf crude exports and inventory depletion absorption

facts.claim: Average crude exports from the Persian Gulf plus re-routed volumes over the last ten days have recovered to about 19 million barrels per day, just 3 million barrels per day below pre-war levels.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: Strait of Hormuz reopening and logistical recovery

facts.claim: Floating crude storage has fallen to just 20 million barrels, while another 10 million barrels remain in onshore tanks awaiting export.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: Backlog of stranded cargoes exiting storage post-conflict

facts.claim: Since the start of the Middle East conflict, the world has lost roughly 11.7 million barrels per day of supply.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure

facts.claim: Approximately 5.3 million barrels per day of the conflict-induced supply loss was absorbed through demand loss.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: High oil prices during conflict period

facts.claim: China's collapse in oil demand and imports accounted for nearly one-third of the entire global adjustment to the conflict supply shock.
facts.subject: China
facts.cause: Price-driven demand destruction and reduced refinery runs

facts.claim: Dubai crude, the grade favored by Chinese refiners, is currently trading near $66 per barrel.
facts.subject: Dubai crude

facts.claim: During the conflict, Chinese crude imports fell to their lowest levels since late 2016.
facts.subject: China
facts.cause: Conflict-related demand destruction and high prices

facts.claim: JP Morgan estimates China's oil demand to decline by 600,000 barrels per day in 2026 before rebounding by 800,000 barrels per day in 2027.
facts.subject: China
facts.cause: Temporary demand destruction from conflict, followed by recovery as prices normalize

facts.claim: JP Morgan expects first signs of a crude oil surplus to emerge in August when Hormuz flows recover to about 93%, with oversupply estimated at 1.2 million barrels per day initially.
facts.subject: Crude oil
facts.cause: Rapid recovery of Persian Gulf production exceeding recovery in Chinese demand

facts.claim: JP Morgan projects crude oil oversupply to widen to nearly 4 million barrels per day by the final quarter of 2026 and average 3 million barrels per day in 2027.
facts.subject: Crude oil
